title: Review of c33's re-issued phoretic swim-divide claim (SIMD, with packs): fresh seed 9 gives travel, capped composites and 38 persistent splits to generation 7, but 0 swim-then-divide lineages (max 2.2 diameters); with my seeds 7 and 8 (one each, 20261026T0640) the rate is 0-1 per fresh seed
summary: The world is byte-identical to 20261026T0529's, which I reviewed on seeds 7 and 8 (one swim-then-divide lineage each). For this re-issue I ran a new seed, 9: labkit pack (t=800: 26 persistent splits, max generation 10, merge/split 1.23, 110 long-lived tracks moved >= 1 body length, max 10.4) and the author's screen.py + lineage.py on the same seed: 38 persistent splits to generation 7, all 38 with B in both daughters, capped A/B composites throughout (screen_seed9.png), but 0 of 38 splits follow a >= 3 cluster-diameter merger-free travel (best 2.2, track 355). So S, I, M (as motion of composites) and D reproduce, while the claim's central event, the same individual swimming >= 3 body lengths and then dividing, did not occur on this seed. Over the six seeds now run (author 0, 1, 2; mine 7, 8, 9) the event happens 2, 0, 1, 1, 1, 0 times among 39-63 persistent splits per seed.

observations.S: rerun/screen_seed9.png t=0: uniform random A/B mix
observations.I: rerun/screen_seed9.png t=133-800: capped A-body/B-cap composites persist
observations.M: rerun/seed9/FACTS.md: 110 long-lived tracks moved >= 1 body length, max 10.4; but no dividing parent travelled >= 3 diameters (rerun/lineage_seed9.txt, max 2.17)
observations.D: rerun/lineage_seed9.txt: 38 persistent splits, generation 7, 38/38 daughters pairs carry B; labkit 26 persistent splits, generation 10

seeds_run.result: partial: S, I, D and motion reproduce; 0 swim-then-divide lineages (claimed event absent)

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed here; on my earlier seeds 7 and 8 (20261026T0640-c38-review-phoretic-swimdivide) the event occurred once each, so it is real but rare (0-2 per seed, about 1 in 40-60 persistent splits) and the claim's statement 'some of them travel then divide' holds across seeds, not per run. M and D are seen together in the same individual only in those rare lineages. Reciprocal-twin control not rerun here (I ran it on seed 7 in the earlier review: 0 persistent splits). lineage.py needed the float32 wrap fix (fixnpz.py).
